seed.name: glycogen storage disease due to glycogen branching enzyme deficiency

partners.mechanism_chain: GBE1 (HGNC:4180) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen branching (GO:0005997); Glycogen branching (GO:0005997) —DECREASES→ Abnormal glycogen structure (CHEBI:24373); Abnormal glycogen structure (CHEBI:24373) —LEADS_TO→ Accumulation of polyglucosan bodies (HP:0030111); Abnormal glycogen structure (CHEBI:24373) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatomegaly (HP:0002240); Abnormal glycogen structure (CHEBI:24373) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252). Loss-of-function mutations in GBE1 impair its ability to create alpha-1,6-branch linkages in glycogen. This leads to the formation of abnormally long, unbranched glycogen chains (polyglucosan bodies), which accumulate in various tissues, causing the phenotypes observed in both diseases.

partners.mechanism_chain: GBE1 (HGNC:4276) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen synthesis and branching; Glycogen synthesis and branching —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal glycogen accumulation (HP:0003692); GYG1 (HGNC:24137) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen breakdown and remodeling; Glycogen breakdown and remodeling —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003198). Loss-of-function mutations in GBE1 disrupt glycogen synthesis and branching, leading to abnormal glycogen accumulation (Disease A). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in GYG1 disrupt glycogen breakdown and remodeling, contributing to polyglucosan body formation and myopathy (Disease B). While distinct genes are involved, both pathways converge on the cellular processes of glycogen metabolism and storage, ultimately leading to distinct but related pathological phenotypes.
